items.title: Brand-New $399 Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Release Officially Revealed
items.summary: Fans of one of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.content:
Brand-New $399 Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Release Officially Revealed From GameRant (Written by James Ratcliff) on November 16, 2026 | OpenCritic

The 2025 game of the year, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , has teamed up with Pix'n Love Games for an official new statue release featuring Monoco that is available to pre-order for $400 as of this writing. As the only officially licensed Expedition 33 statue of its kind so far, the Monoco statue is expected to launch by the end of 2026.

Following its April 2025 release across the globe, Expedition 33 received universal acclaim for its turn-based RPG gameplay, its gripping main story, and vocal performances from its star-studded cast. The hit RPG from France-based Sandfall Interactive went on to win several end-of-year accolades from different media outlets, including a record-setting nine awards during The Game Awards 2025. President of France Emmanuel Macron personally congratulated Sandfall following its award-winning sweep, calling it a "historic first" for the French gaming industry.

Eagle-eyed GTA 6 fans spot a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Easter egg in the latest gameplay footage.

Soon, fans of the popular turn-based RPG can add a new collectible statue to their shelves. A 1/6 scale statue of Monoco from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available for pre-order for €399.90...

items.title: These are the 100 greatest gaming themes, according to a new orchestral album
items.summary: A new album featuring orchestral reimaginings of the 100 greatest gaming themes has been released onto streaming
items.content:
Gaming News These are the 100 greatest gaming themes, according to a new orchestral album Featuring musical moments from ‘The Legend Of Zelda’, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’, ‘Red Dead Redemption’, ‘God Of War’ and more By Ali Shutler | 16th November 2026 ‘Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’. CREDIT: Sandfall

A new album featuring orchestral reimaginings of the 100 greatest gaming themes has been released onto streaming.

READ MORE: AI, vinyl and indie supremacy: what’s shaping video game music in 2026?

Organised by Silva Screen Records and performed by London Music Works, the ‘100 Greatest Video Game Themes’ album features a stacked tracklisting of epic musical gaming moments.

The collection opens with ‘Lumière’ from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and features themes from Hogwarts Legacy , Tetris , Death Stranding , Red Dead Redemption 2 , God Of War , The Last Of Us and Tomb Raider .

There are also a medley of different Pokemon themes included on ‘100 Greatest Video Game Themes’ as well as music from 17 different The Legend Of Zelda titles.

“London Music Works is a collective of talented musicians based in London, specialising in performing music from films, TV series, and video games,” explains a press release. “Since its inception, the ensemble has become a leading force in reinterpreting iconic orchestral scores, often working closely with original composers. Through their exceptional recording quality and precise performances, London Music Works has captivated audiences worldwide, bringing a new dimension to both classic and contemporary screen music.”

This year alone, the collective have released albums paying tribute to Studio Ghibli movies, The Last Of Us video games and The Elder Scrolls series.

There’s no word yet on whether Silva Screen Records will be giving ‘100 Greatest Video Game Themes’ a vinyl release, though previous gaming soundtracks have gotten a full physical launch.

Last week, Nintendo added more dates to its ‘ The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Concert’ series after a majority of tickets sold out instantly. Kicking off in January, the tour will visit Europe, North America, Asia and Australia over the next 12 months. As part of the run, ‘The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Concert’ will play five nights at London’s Royal Albert Hall.

items.title: The 2026 GOTY Race Could Be a Disaster for Indie Games
items.summary: After three indie nominees last year, this year’s leading contender is in trouble
items.content:
By Oli Welsh Published Nov 15, 2026, 12:00 PM EST Oli Welsh has been covering the business and culture of video games for two decades. He started out writing for Edge and other publications (specializing in MMOs and Blizzard, as cover for his World of Warcraft playtime) before joining Eurogamer, where he worked for 14 years as reviews editor, deputy editor, and editor-in-chief; Eurogamer won many Games Media Awards during his tenure. At Polygon, he writes about film and TV as well as games, and provides news, analysis, and criticism on the entertainment we love and the industries that make it, all from his home in London. He loves role-playing, racing, puzzles, tactics, exploration, storytelling, Nintendo, mysteries, spies, fantasy, reality, cars, and classic cinema. He wanted to be a movie critic when he grew up, and now he’s definitely grown up, and occasionally is one. He considers this a win. GOTY Watch After three indie nominees last year, this year’s leading contender is in trouble

Image: House House/Panic via Polygon Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 3 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Last year was a watershed moment for indie games at The Game Awards . Three games were nominated for both Game of the Year and Best Independent Game: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , Hades 2 , and Hollow Knight: Silksong . Together, they made up half of the GOTY 2025 field.

Some quibble with the definition of Clair Obscur , a sizable production, as an indie game. (For what it's worth, the studio that made it is independent, and its publisher Kepler Interactive was founded by a collective of indie studios; it's definitely culturally indie.) But even if you excluded it, this was still the first time more than one game had crossed over between the indie and GOTY categories in the history of the awards.

If you interpret this result as a sure sign that The Game Awards is taking indie games much more seriously, I'm afraid you might be disappointed. The 2025 nominations flatter to deceive, and 2026 looks like it will be a different matter. All three 2025 indie GOTY nominees were huge sellers, and two of them were high-profile sequels to critical darlings and popular favorites. These were not normal times. In previous years things were much more patchy. Balatro , 2024's indie nominee, was a massive viral hit. There was no indie nominee in 2023. In 2022, the lucky game was the distinctly slick and mainstream Stray . Prior to that, one indie game would typically break through every other year.

Increasing recognition of indie games among the critical community has been counterbalanced by the international expansion of The Game Awards jury . This expansion has tended to flatten the jury's taste , and tends to disadvantage indie developers who can't afford localization into multiple languages — not an issue for 2025's three big beasts.

So we turn to the 2026 race. There have been some superb and well-reviewed indie games this year, as there are every year: Big Walk , Mina the Hollower , Zero Parades , Mewgenics , Cairn , Denshattack! , Mixtape . None of them have been hits on the scale of the last few indie nominees, however, nor have they penetrated the culture in the same way as 2025’s games.

Image: Yacht Club Games Nevertheless, a nomination for one of them is still in prospect, because this year's GOTY slate is relatively weak , with many evenly matched titles fighting over the few nomination slots left after dead certs Grand Theft Auto 6 , The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , and Resident Evil Requiem are accounted for. In those circumstances, there's a path to nomination for an indie game with a stellar critical reputation and strong support.

The best candidates are Mina the Hollower and Big Walk , both critical darlings with 90-plus ratings on Metacritic. Mina was more widely covered at launch, but didn't click with a big audience. As a multiplayer co-op game, Big Walk has had a longer tail in the conversation, and has more viral stickiness. Jury members have probably been playing it over time with their friend groups. It's been my pick of the two so far, and its case was buoyed by a win in the Critic's Choice category at this week's Golden Joystick Awards .

However, also this week, developer House House made the disastrous admission that generative AI had been used to write some code for Big Walk . This will likely rule the game out of contention for several indie awards, like the IGF and Indie Game Awards. (The Indie Game Awards stripped Clair Obscur of its 2025 Game of the Year award over use of generative AI.) Its impact on Big Walk 's fortunes at The Game Awards is less clear.

Image: House House/Panic The broad-church Game Awards jury is likely less swayed by ethical issues such as AI usage than small, indie-specialist juries. That said, Big Walk will need the whole indie-fan coalition within The Game Awards jury to rally around it if it's going to get a nomination. An added wrinkle is that the AI news hit toward the final stage of The Game Awards' two-step nomination process. Jury members offended by the AI usage would have to actively remove Big Walk nominations they'd already made, rather than just not make them.

The controversy might not hurt Big Walk 's chances as much as you might think, But it certainly doesn't help them. In a tight race for those final nominations, the leading indie contender just took a big knock. Can Mina the Hollower take up the mantle? Or will Big Walk 's loss be some AAA title's gain — Control Resonant , perhaps, or 007 First Light ? We'll find out soon enough.

What’s in pole position for gaming’s top prize? Let’s make some predictions

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33

items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Introducing a special bundle featuring the award‑winning fantasy RPG “Metaphor: ReFantazio”, created by the team behind Persona 3-5, paired with “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33” - now available at 10% off!

Enjoy both titles and experience the worlds for yourself!

The Metaphor: ReFantazio × Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Bundle includes two games: “Metaphor: ReFantazio” and “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.”

Message from Guillaume Broche & Katsura Hashino

"Metaphor: ReFantazio is a game that is really inspiring for us. It tells a beautiful story in a completely new world that is masterfully crafted. It deals with heavy themes but one that resonates strongly with me is the importance of imagination in all aspects of our lives. The cast is lovable and the turn-based battle system is one of the best I have played. The re-imagination of the traditional jobs system through Archetypes is fantastic and opens up so many playstyles that are fun to play around with. On top of that, the game has one of the most charismatic villains I've ever seen in an RPG. It is a great honor to be able to collaborate with Atlus on this bundle, as I have been a fan of their work since Shin Megami Tensei: Lucifer's Call (also known as Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne for some players)." - Guillaume Broche

"I am Katsura Hashino from ATLUS, serving as the Creative Director for “Metaphor: ReFantazio.” I am very pleased to hear that a Steam bundle will be released with “Expedition 33,” a title that has received high praise around the world.

“Expedition 33” is a work that conveys a deep understanding of and sincere dedication to the JRPG genre, crafted with great care down to the finest details. As someone who also creates RPGs, I found it to be truly inspiring.

I am genuinely delighted to see Japanese-style RPGs being born and embraced, not only from Japanese-based studios like ours, but other places around the world through diverse creative approaches.

While the two titles differ in their worlds and overall direction, players may find a shared spirit in how we each approach and express the RPG genre. I hope that this bundle encourages players to experience both titles and enjoy the breadth of what RPGs can offer."

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 | Dev Blog - Photo Mode
items.summary: Expeditioners, We're so pleased to see so many of you enjoying the new photo mode feature!! We put a lot of time and care into building this feature and we’re so glad to see so many of you enjoying it! There were a lot of moving parts invol
items.content:
Expeditioners,

We're so pleased to see so many of you enjoying the new photo mode feature!!

We put a lot of time and care into building this feature and we’re so glad to see so many of you enjoying it! There were a lot of moving parts involved in getting the Photo Mode set up, so we thought we’d show a bit of the process in this blog and talk a bit about what went into building this feature.

There were a few key people involved in the development of this, and each of them had a part to write here !

VINCENT CONSTANTIN-TURKI – Producer \

One of the main features we wanted to introduce with the Thank You Update was Photo Mode. It felt like a meaningful way to give something back to the players and thank them for their commitment to the game.

What’s funny is that the team in charge of developing Photo Mode doesn’t usually use this feature in other games, which is why we decided to collaborate with Shinobi. He helped us design a Photo Mode that would truly resonate with players.

NAJA DALMAGNE – QA Coordinator \

In many games we tested, Photo Modes often felt restrictive, which could quickly become frustrating. So, from the very beginning, one of the key goals we all agreed on was to give players as much freedom as possible. It was really about letting players express their creativity without getting in the way.

During development, the QA team ran into some unexpected and sometimes quite funny issues. One of the funniest, but also one of the most severe, involved characters whose heads or torsos could become displaced or deformed when opening the Photo Mode if they hadn’t been visible on screen for a while during exploration.

One feature I’m particularly proud of is the lighting system Florian worked on. It offers great flexibility while remaining fairly easy to use, which really makes a difference when you're trying to get the perfect shot.

FLORIAN TORRES – Senior Gameplay Programmer \ \

I love giving players as many tools and features as possible (that’s literally the purpose of my job).

When we started working on the photo mode, our goal was to give players as few restrictions as possible and that’s what I was in charge of coding: infinite camera distance, the ability to pass through collisions, lots of customizable lights, many (weird) filters, and more.

Of course, that comes with its challenges, but in the end it allows players to see a lot of things we don’t want to show during normal gameplay. The photo mode became a way to peek behind the scenes of each cinematic or environment, and sometimes even see how we have created the entire game.

Ever wondered what happens outside the camera frame? Here’s an example (sorry cinematic team, I love you).

LUDOVIC ‘SHINOBI’ HELME – Photo Mode Consultant \

We felt it was important to include anything that increases the “freedom” factor for players. It opens up countless possibilities every time someone enters photo mode: a very generous camera range to capture unseen details or create epic compositions, RGB curves control to edit and build your own color schemes, a strong custom lighting system to truly take ownership of a scene, and solid depth-of-field management.

But when all of that is also available in cutscenes - giving access to those incredible facial expressions and emotions - that’s when I really start to feel satisfied.

Every shot I’ve seen has blown my mind, and I often wish I’d been the one to come up with the idea. It’s truly inspiring.

I’m very proud that the team managed to create a tool that is both beginner-friendly and deeply satisfying for more experienced photographers. Finding that balance is extremely difficult.

With all of these features, there had to be a user-friendly way for people to make use of everything. Making sure players had full control of all the settings and could navigate all the features comes down to our awesome Gameplay & UI Programmer, VICTOR BOULEZ.

Thank you for all of your appreciation and feedback on this feature, we had a lot of fun making it and even more fun watching you use it!

This past week, especially, we’ve really loved the work you’ve all been putting into the social Photo Mode Prompt Challenge!! We’ve seen some amazing photography this past week, it’s completely blown our minds how creative you have been able to get with the prompts and tools.

Even though the challenge is over, feel free to keep sharing your work with us on social media, we thoroughly enjoy seeing some of your masterpieces!!

In the meantime, we are continuing to work on fixes for ongoing problems, keep an eye on the bug thread and socials to stay updated on the latest.

Finally, we leave you with some of our favourite uses of photo mode.

items.title: I played Cory in the House for Nintendo DS to find out if it’s truly better than Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: I played the Disney game threatening Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s top Metacritic ranking — is it actually good?
items.content:

That’s a name I haven’t heard in a long time. See, this 2008-released ‘adventure stealth’ game – as well as the TV show it’s based on – has been a meme for more than a decade. In the past, I’d often see Cory in the House being described as the ‘best anime of all time’. I’d also read Amazon reviews of the video game, which would hail it as a true ‘masterpiece’.

And now, in 2026, the meme seems to have been reborn. Users have taken to Metacritic and flooded it with positive reviews for Cory in the House on the Nintendo DS. And now, its user score sits at 9.3, which is indicative of ‘universal acclaim’. That score is so high, in fact, that the title is genuinely posing a threat to the top-ranked game on Metacritic by user score. And that game is none other than TechRadar’s Game of the Year of 2025, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

After hearing all of this, you may be wondering: is Cory in the House on Nintendo DS actually good? Well, it’s your lucky day. See, back in my teens, a friend of mine jokingly gifted me the game for Christmas, and thankfully, I still own it to this day. So, I dusted the cartridge off, put it in my Nintendo 3DS console, and played through it for the very first time. Here’s what I made of my time with the ‘universally acclaimed’ title.

My game card didn’t work at first, but after a few blows and re-insertions, I was finally in. When I reached the main menu, there were a few options to choose from, including Story, an arcade mode, and a gallery. I got straight into the Story mode, and well…it was quite something.

In this campaign, you play as Cory Baxter, a teenager whose dad works as the head chef at The White House. As an aspiring businessman, Cory decides to sell bobbleheads of the President to the people of Washington DC – but trouble is afoot. See, an evil toymaker has turned the bobbleheads into hypnotic devices, and it’s your job to foil their malign scheme. Ridiculous? Absolutely. But I came into this experience with an open heart and an open mind.

I wasn't convinced by Elden Ring Tarnished Edition until I played it on Nintendo Switch 2 Final Fantasy Resonance review: classic RPG greatness made for 2026 Dark Souls is nothing compared to this: I wasn’t expecting a Mii to push me to my limits in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, but this one boss battle had me absolutely raging However, as soon as I got into the game, I was instantly struck by frankly horrifying visuals. No, really, I have a feeling Cory’s face will be haunting my nightmares for the foreseeable future. See, characters are so unrefined and blurred that you can’t even see their eyes or expressions. And that’s not inherent to the console – plenty of DS games pulled off nice-looking character models in spite of the handheld’s technical limitations.

Anyway, that’s not the end of the world, at least the gameplay could still be fun! Right? Well, I suppose in a sense, Cory in the House truly is a genre-defining title; in that it defines exactly how not to make an adventure stealth game. Movement is janky, throwing exploding fictional pastries is, somehow, totally mind-numbing, and the various settings are unbelievably bland. You play the occasional mini-game to progress the story, but even these are so laughably basic that I can’t even imagine a child having fun.

Oh, and one more thing. You have a lot of conversations with characters like Cory’s father, bandmates, and store workers – many of which are intended to be funny…at least I think they are? Sometimes I was unsure whether Cory was trying to crack a joke, but luckily, a laugh track would play when it was time for me to giggle. Artificial laughs even seem to play when characters don’t say anything remotely funny, which in itself was actually kinda entertaining. So, I guess there’s that?

So, there you have it, folks. Cory in the House for the Nintendo DS is – in spite of its 9.3 user score on Metacritic – a pretty terrible TV show tie-in, and it’s no wonder that its two critic review scores are listed as a 30 and a 40. Ouch.

Still, I’ve been finding the explosion of ironic meme-fuelled positive reviews pretty funny, even as a massive lover of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . And while we’re here, it only seems right to recommend this actual masterpiece to anyone who hasn’t tried it yet.

Tales of Eternia Remastered review: a real blast from the past After parting ways with Xbox, I pray that Double Fine is working on more games like Psychonauts 2 — one of the best platformers since Super Mario Odyssey Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave review: the best game on Nintendo Switch 2 so far Yes, Expedition 33 is a phenomenal RPG, with one of the best stories that’s ever been told through the video game medium, in my view. It plates up incredibly addictive gameplay, with an excellent parrying mechanic that’s a joy to master. Combine that with a jaw-droppingly gorgeous visual style and generational soundtrack, and it’s simply a must-play.

No matter how good it is, though, it may not be able to stop the immovable force that is Cory in the House for the Nintendo DS, which, in its own ‘special’ way, is a game that I won’t be forgetting in a hurry.

items.title: 'There is a bit of pressure': Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs will stay true to themselves for their next game despite expectations—'we need to trust our instincts'
items.content:
RPG Clair Obscur Expedition 33 'There is a bit of pressure': Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs will stay true to themselves for their next game despite expectations—'we need to trust our instincts' News By Elie Gould Published 5 January 2026 I'd be excited no matter what happens, honestly.

a]:text-inherit [&>a]:underline"> When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Sandfall Interactive) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs have had a pretty impressive year. Releasing to almost entirely glowing reviews, it has since gone on to sweep awards and even received two public shout-outs from French President Emmanuel Macron . But as one chapter ends, another begins as the Sandfall devs prepare for their next game.

Talking to Edge magazine for issue 419 , Sandfall Interactive's chief operating officer and production director, François Meurisse, explained the angst and thought process behind stepping into the next game (via GamesRadar ).

"There is a bit of pressure" from fans and critics when it comes to the team's next game, but "it's not so important to us," Meurisse explains. "We have time to get really focused on the next game. We have some great ideas we're so excited to explore, and we don't start from the same point. The team already has five more years of experience. So maybe we can do some great stuff."

That's a rather humble reflection. While there's never any guarantee a game will do better than the last or even live up to expectations, and while I understand why Sandfall may want to downplay its next game while it's still in its conceptual stage, this studio has proved without a doubt that it's capable of truly amazing things. It managed to persuade a bunch of us here at PC Gamer that parrying is actually a hell of a lot of fun , well done.

But the making of Sandfall's next game will undoubtedly be different from its first, not least because the studio now has a reputation and a bunch of eager fans. That fact is not lost on lead writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen: "[I'm] a bit of a people pleaser, so it's always in the back of my mind that we have a lot of fans now, and they have certain expectations and certain feelings towards the game. I'd be lying if I said that I didn't think about that at all."

Former Arkane vets' new studio isn't going to try 'trend chasing', and in hindsight, thank God Dishonored 2 director Harvey Smith wants to honour sacred imsim texts while finding new ways to surprise fans: 'That's the two wolves inside me' Ex-BioWare designer says doom and gloom about the next Mass Effect is overstated: 'I think that they can do it' But despite the weight of expectations hanging over the studio, it seems like the devs are planning to stay steadfast in their creative autonomy. "Creatively, we've always let our North Star be our own personal taste in terms of what we think is cool, what it is we enjoy and want to see," Svedberg-Yen says. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process, you end up losing the heart of what's there. So [we] feel like we need to trust our instincts and continue to trust the vision behind the studio."

items.title: Hotfix 1.5.1 is live!
items.summary: Bug Fixes & Improvements Expeditioners, the 1.5.1 hotfix is now live! Thanks to your reports, we have worked on a number of fixes listed below: Gameplay Fixed Monoco’s weapon “Cannaro” being unobtainable from Chromatic Machinapieds Players
items.content:
Bug Fixes & Improvements

Expeditioners, the 1.5.1 hotfix is now live!

Thanks to your reports, we have worked on a number of fixes listed below:

Gameplay

  • Fixed Monoco’s weapon “Cannaro” being unobtainable from Chromatic Machinapieds

    • Players who already defeated the boss will automatically receive the weapon in their inventory, unless they started a NG+(+) after that

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed Esquim not applying Mark to all enemies when a skill had 0 hits.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a targeting issue caused by using a Recoat item followed by ‘Retry Battle’, which resulted in the player being unable to target the middle enemy or character.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft-lock when attempting to load a save without hovering any slot while backup saves were displayed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed upgrade of the weapons to level 34 when spamming Upgrade weapon and change character buttons

    • Level 34 weapons have been reverted back to level 33

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed character being able to use other characters' weapon when quickly switching weapon tabs after changing weapon

    [/*]

Environment

  • Nerfed the hardest boss in Verso’s Drafts (red lifebuoy) by moving it slightly to make a quest easier.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

Audio & Music

  • Improved environmental ambiances and spatial audio for better immersion in Verso’s Drafts

    [/*]

  • Enhanced audio mixes for select characters, combos, and finishers

    [/*]

  • Multiple audio & music issues were resolved, including:

    • Missing music after defeating new Endless Tower bosses.

      [/*]

    • Missing subtitle line for Sciel in one of the new cinematics.

      [/*]

    • Missing Barbapapa status effect SFX when receiving a second stack.

      [/*]

    • Missing some SFX for Licorne enemy in Verso’s Drafts.

      [/*]

    • Missing SFX for Paint Cage explosions in Verso's Drafts.

      [/*]

    • Music and SFX not pausing when opening pause menu during cinematic sequence with slow motion enabled, resulting in audio desynchronization for the remainder of the cinematic sequence

      [/*]
    [/*]

Localization

Fixed various localization issues, including:

  • Subtitles in Root Of All Evil cinematics disappearing too fast.

    [/*]

  • Overlapping text in Pictos & Luminas lists.

    [/*]

  • Autoplay dialogue options swapped when the title is set to LATAM Spanish.

    [/*]

  • Incorrect text displayed during Flying Manor side quest when the title is set to Vietnamese.

    [/*]

  • Verso’s skill Phantom Stars displaying HTML in combat when the title is set to Vietnamese.

    [/*]

Other

We are aware of various issues encountered, particularly the one reported by some of you who are having difficulty launching the title on Windows 11.

One of these issues is caused by Windows Security reporting false positives when launching. This has been fixed as part of the v1.5.1 hotfix as of 17:00 CET.

The other issue causing this problem is related to the Windows Smart App Control feature. Turning it off to fix it is not recommended as this will remove the feature permanently from your system. We are investigating this issue and hope to resolve it as soon as possible so we suggest waiting for the next hotfix!

Until then, 

Tomorrow comes!

And as always thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform!

~ The Expedition 33 Team 

Update 08/01

We've pushed a fix for the soft lock occurring when Braseleur hits the player with orbs during two consecutive enemy turns.

items.content:
What an incredible night at The Game Awards!!

Congratulations to ALL of our fellow nominees and winners tonight - we're so happy to be part of an incredible evening! 

To celebrate this amazing year, and as a sincere ‘Thank You’ to the community, we are now rolling out the free major ‘Thank You’ Update, adding new content and a few fun surprises!

  You can expect to find: 

  • A new, playable environment, taking the characters to new adventures... 

    [/*]

  • Brand new music tracks by award-winning composer, Lorien Testard. 

    [/*]

  • Challenging boss battles for late-game players to overcome within the Endless Tower. 

    [/*]

  • An official Photo Mode, allowing players to get creative and capture their favourite moments from the game’s story and battles. 

    [/*]

  • New text and UI game localizations into Czech, Ukrainian, Latin American Spanish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Thai, and Indonesian, bringing the total number of supported languages to 19. 

    [/*]

  • New Quality of Life improvements, other new features, and additional improvements to the game’s performance across platforms, including on handheld PC systems.

    [/*]

Read the full patch notes here:

And of course, new music tracks by the wonderful Lorien Testard are available on digital streaming platforms now, so let your neighbours know they’ll have to listen through the walls.

https://lnk.to/exp33-versos-drafts

Our gratitude for this community goes far beyond what we are able to express, but this update should hopefully serve as our way of saying thank you. 

This year has truly been incredible thanks to you. <3
